code.router.http.why: Get a correct response for each request it sends to a path with a method.
code.router.http.how: The router matches the request path and method, calls the registered handler, and returns its response.

code.router.http.why: Get a correct response for each request it sends to a path with a method.
code.router.http.how: The router matches the request path and method, calls the registered handler, and returns its response.

code.router.method.why: Pick the endpoint for the request method once the path has matched.
code.router.method.how: Each registered path holds a MethodRouter that dispatches by method, adds HEAD from GET, and answers 405 with an Allow header.

upstream.library.routing_trie.why: Match a request path to a registered route and extract path parameters and wildcards.
upstream.library.routing_trie.how: Router keeps a matchit tree; route, nest and merge insert paths, and each request does one lookup that returns a route id and parameters.

code.handler.request.why: Produce the response for a request whose path and method matched.
code.handler.request.how: Stores one boxed endpoint per HTTP method (get, post, on, any) built from a Handler, and calls it with the request and state.

code.middleware.why: Wrap only the endpoints of one path with extra behavior.
code.middleware.how: route_layer and layer wrap each stored method endpoint with a tower Layer; the layer applies only when the method matched.

code.handler.error.why: Turn an endpoint's service error into a response so the router stays infallible.
code.handler.error.how: handle_error wraps the endpoints with a user function that maps the error to an IntoResponse value.

code.extractor.request.why: Build each handler argument from the incoming request before the handler body runs.
code.extractor.request.how: The Handler impl for functions takes up to 16 arguments; all but the last implement FromRequestParts, and the last implements FromRequest and may consume the body.

upstream.library.core.why: Turn the handler's return value into an HTTP response, including Html, NoContent, status codes, headers and tuples.
upstream.library.core.how: The return type must implement IntoResponse, defined in axum-core.

code.response.redirect.why: Send the client to another location.
code.response.redirect.how: A handler returns Redirect (to, temporary, permanent), which sets the status and Location header.

code.stream.event.why: Push a live sequence of events to the client over one response.
code.stream.event.how: A handler returns Sse wrapping a Stream of Event values, with optional keep-alive comments.

upstream.library.core.why: Define the extraction contract and rejection handling.
upstream.library.core.how: Implements FromRequest and FromRequestParts traits, OptionalFromRequest, FromRef and DefaultBodyLimit from axum-core; rejection types convert to responses.

upstream.library.http_types.why: Read request parts: method, URI, headers, extensions and body.

code.router.http.why: Receive the named path parameters captured while matching the route.
code.router.http.how: The router stores percent-decoded parameters in the request extensions as UrlParams; Path deserializes them into a tuple, map, or struct with serde.

upstream.library.http_types.how: Query deserializes the query string of the request URI into a user type with serde_urlencoded.

code.router.http.why: Receive the application state the router holds.
code.router.http.how: with_state supplies the state; State<T> clones it, or a part of it through FromRef, into the handler argument.

upstream.library.core.why: Read and limit the request body, and reject bad input.
upstream.library.core.how: Json, Form and Multipart check Content-Type, buffer the body within DefaultBodyLimit, deserialize it, and return a rejection response on failure. Json and Form also serialize as responses.

code.server.http.why: Learn the remote peer address or other per-connection data.
code.server.http.how: into_make_service_with_connect_info makes the server insert a ConnectInfo<C> extension built from each IncomingStream.

upstream.library.http_protocol.why: Complete a WebSocket handshake and take over the connection.
upstream.library.http_protocol.how: Validates the upgrade headers, replies 101 with the accept key, and runs the user callback with the upgraded hyper connection (feature ws).

upstream.library.core.how: Json, Form and Multipart check Content-Type, buffer the body within DefaultBodyLimit, deserialize it, and return a rejection response on failure. Json and Form also serialize as responses.

code.server.http.how: into_make_service_with_connect_info makes the server insert a ConnectInfo<C> extension built from each IncomingStream.

upstream.library.http_protocol.how: Validates the upgrade headers, replies 101 with the accept key, and runs the user callback with the upgraded hyper connection (feature ws).

code.handler.request.why: Answer requests that match no route, and requests to a nested path without a handler.
code.handler.request.how: fallback and method_not_allowed_fallback store a Handler that the router calls when the trie lookup or the method lookup fails; the default is an empty 404.

code.middleware.why: Apply cross-cutting behavior to all routes or to the fallback.
code.middleware.how: layer wraps every route and the fallback, route_layer wraps only matched routes; the layer is any tower Layer or an axum middleware adapter.

upstream.library.service.why: Accept any tower Service as an endpoint and be a Service itself so it composes with other tower code.
upstream.library.service.how: route_service, nest_service and fallback_service take Services; Router implements Service<Request> and into_make_service gives a MakeService.

code.extractor.state.why: Hold the shared application state and give it to every handler and middleware.
code.extractor.state.how: Router<S> is generic over missing state; with_state(state) fixes S and passes a clone to each call.

upstream.library.service.why: Wrap an inner Service and expose the wrapper as a tower Layer.
upstream.library.service.how: from_fn, map_request, map_response and from_extractor build FromFnLayer, MapRequestLayer and similar types that implement tower Layer and Service; from_fn passes the request on through Next.

code.extractor.request.why: Give the middleware function typed access to request data.
code.extractor.request.how: Middleware functions take FromRequestParts arguments before the Request, and from_extractor runs an extractor as a gate that rejects the request or lets it continue.

upstream.library.service.why: Catch the error type of a fallible tower Service.
upstream.library.service.how: HandleErrorLayer and HandleError wrap a Service whose Error is not Infallible and call a user function with the error and extracted arguments.

code.extractor.request.why: Let the error function read request data.
code.extractor.request.how: The error function may take FromRequestParts arguments before the error value.

code.listener.connection.how: serve takes any Listener, loops on accept, and for each connection builds an IncomingStream and calls the make-service with it.

code.router.http.why: Hand each parsed request to the application and send back its response.
code.router.http.how: serve takes a Router (through into_make_service) as the make-service; each connection gets a clone that handles its requests.

upstream.library.http_protocol.why: Parse HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 on each connection.
upstream.library.http_protocol.how: Uses hyper-util auto::Builder serve_connection_with_upgrades with a TowerToHyperService adapter.

upstream.runtime.async.why: Spawn one task per connection and end gracefully on a signal.
upstream.runtime.async.how: tokio::spawn per connection; with_graceful_shutdown waits for a user future, then stops accepting and drains open connections.
Implemented for tokio TcpListener and UnixListener; accept returns an io stream and its address, and handles transient accept errors.

upstream.library.http_types.why: Set the redirect status and Location header.
upstream.library.http_types.how: Builds a response with StatusCode 303, 307 or 308 and a HeaderValue location.

upstream.runtime.async.why: Time the keep-alive comments between events.
upstream.runtime.async.how: KeepAliveStream uses a tokio Sleep to send a comment line after the configured interval of silence.

upstream.library.core.why: Send the stream as a response body.
upstream.library.core.how: Sse implements IntoResponse with content type text/event-stream and a streaming Body.

code.middleware.why: Receive values that earlier layers stored for later handlers.
code.middleware.how: An Extension layer (AddExtension) inserts a cloneable value into request extensions; Extension<T> reads it and rejects with 500 when absent.

code.router.http.why: Receive the named path parameters and the route information captured while matching.
code.router.http.how: The router stores percent-decoded parameters in the request extensions as UrlParams; Path deserializes them into a tuple, map, or struct with serde. The same extensions give MatchedPath (the route pattern), NestedPath (the nest prefix) and OriginalUri (the URI before prefix stripping).

upstream.library.core.why: Read and limit the request body, and reject bad input.
upstream.library.core.how: Json, Form and Multipart check Content-Type, buffer the body within DefaultBodyLimit, deserialize it, and return a rejection response on failure. RawForm and RawQuery give the undecoded text. Json and Form also serialize as responses.

upstream.library.routing_trie.why: Match a request path to a registered route and extract path parameters and wildcards.
upstream.library.routing_trie.how: Router keeps a matchit tree; route, nest and merge insert paths, and each request does one lookup that returns a route id and parameters. A nested router is inserted under a prefix with a wildcard, and strip_prefix removes the prefix before the inner router sees the URI.

code.extractor.path.how: A handler argument Path<T> deserializes captured route parameters.

code.extractor.query.how: A handler argument Query<T> deserializes the URI query.

code.extractor.body.why: Get the request body as a typed value.
code.extractor.body.how: A last handler argument Json<T>, Form<T> or Multipart consumes the body.

code.extractor.extension.why: Get values that middleware stored on the request.
code.extractor.extension.how: A handler argument Extension<T> clones the stored value.

code.extractor.connect_info.how: A handler argument ConnectInfo<C> reads the value the server stored.

code.extractor.upgrade.how: A handler argument WebSocketUpgrade lets the handler return on_upgrade(callback), a 101 response whose callback owns the socket.

upstream.library.core.why: Turn the handler's return value into an HTTP response.
upstream.library.core.how: The return type must implement IntoResponse, defined in axum-core. axum adds Html, NoContent and Redirect (to: 303, temporary: 307, permanent: 308, with a Location header), and the core covers status codes, headers and tuples.

code.extractor.state.how: A handler argument State<T> clones the state or a FromRef part of it.

upstream.library.router.why: Match a request path to a registered route and extract path parameters and wildcards.
upstream.library.router.how: Router keeps a matchit tree; route, nest and merge insert paths, and each request does one lookup that returns a route id and parameters. A nested router is inserted under a prefix with a wildcard, and strip_prefix removes the prefix before the inner router sees the URI.

code.server.http.why: Receive parsed requests from network connections and return responses to them.
code.server.http.how: serve(listener, router.into_make_service()) accepts connections, parses HTTP, and calls the Router as a tower Service; the Router does not open sockets itself.
